source: Cambodian MAFF/agricultural extension PowerPoint-derived presentation titled "ដំណាំឪឡឹក" (Watermelon), 42 slides; no presenter, publisher, or date named on the slides reviewed. This presentation exists as two near-identical PDF copies in the source set (one with a green-themed slide design, one plain black-on-white reformat of the same 42 slides) - treat as one source, not two corroborating sources.
text:
Watering is guided by soil moisture. When flowering begins, soil moisture should be maintained around 65-70%; if using a drip/furrow irrigation method, water 2 times per week.

Once fruit begins to form and reaches about 5-6cm in size, and the fruit stem/tendril firms up, soil moisture should be maintained higher, around 80-85%, during this fruit-development stage.

Vine training/thinning (ការជ្រុំជ្រាយដី, vine arrangement) is done about 15-17 days after planting, once the young watermelon plant has 6-7 true leaves. At this point, excess leaves are trimmed and the vine is laid out and covered/anchored into the soil to encourage proper vine spread along the ground.
